test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Electrician) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which power loss is assessed by open-circuit test on transformer?
solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Correct Option: Core Loss**

**Definition:** Core loss, also known as iron loss, is the power loss that occurs in the magnetic core of a transformer due to the alternating magnetic field. This loss is primarily composed of hysteresis loss and eddy current loss, which are inherent in the transformer core material when subjected to an AC supply.

**Open-Circuit Test:** The open-circuit test is performed to determine the core loss of a transformer. In this test, the primary winding of the transformer is connected to an AC supply, and the secondary winding is left open (no load condition). A voltmeter, ammeter, and wattmeter are used to measure the applied voltage, current, and power input respectively.

**Procedure:**

 
• The primary winding is energized with its rated voltage while the secondary winding remains open.
 
• Under this condition, the current drawn by the primary winding is very small and is referred to as the no-load current.
 
• The no-load current flows through the transformer and creates an alternating magnetic field in the core.
 
• The power measured by the wattmeter during this test corresponds to the core loss of the transformer.

**Components of Core Loss:**

 
• **Hysteresis Loss:** This loss occurs due to the repeated magnetization and demagnetization of the core material during each cycle of the AC supply. It depends on the material properties of the core and the frequency of the supply.
 
• **Eddy Current Loss:** Eddy currents are induced in the core material due to the alternating magnetic flux. These currents produce heat, causing energy loss. The eddy current loss is proportional to the square of the supply frequency and the thickness of the core laminations.

**Importance of Open-Circuit Test:**

 
• The open-circuit test is essential to assess the core loss, which remains constant irrespective of the transformer load.
 
• It helps in understanding the efficiency of the transformer and is crucial for design optimization.
 
• By minimizing core loss, the overall performance and energy efficiency of the transformer can be improved.
